prompt: Review my branch before I open the PR.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, branch feature/checkout-v2, base origin/main, graph-it installed.
rubric: Runs `git fetch origin main` (or equivalent) so the base ref exists locally
Runs `graph-it review-pr --base origin/main --format markdown` from the repository root
Does not run a separate `graph-it scan` first, because review-pr indexes automatically
Reads risk, score, changedFiles, symbols, limitations and isPartial before concluding
Produces the required output order: verdict, blocking findings, non-blocking findings, test assessment, limitations
anti_patterns: Gives a verdict without citing the command output that supports it
gold_notes: --base is required; --head defaults to HEAD. Output order is part of the contract.

prompt: Here's the review-pr output — can I merge? risk: low, isPartial: true, limitations: ['impact traversal reached depth limit', '2 .py files unsupported'].
rubric: Refuses to call the review complete because isPartial is true and limitations are non-empty
Reports every limitation verbatim or faithfully summarised
Names the manual check that closes each limitation (raise --depth, review the Python files by hand)
Explains that low risk plus partial analysis is not evidence of safety
anti_patterns: Approves the merge on the strength of `risk: low`
Silently drops one of the two limitations
gold_notes: Never complete a review while isPartial is true; signature analysis covers TS/JS extensions only.

prompt: review-pr reports risk: high on updateUser in src/api/users.ts. What now?
context: Repo root: /work/shop, review-pr already run against origin/main.
rubric: Escalates with `graph-it tool get_impact_analysis --filePath=/work/shop/src/api/users.ts --symbolName=updateUser --format=toon`
Also inspects direct callers with get_symbol_callers, or the neighbourhood with query_call_graph --depth=3
Uses absolute paths for every `graph-it tool` file parameter
Maps `high` to the documented action: block until compatibility, callers and tests are addressed
Cites the command output as evidence for each blocking finding
anti_patterns: Speculates about runtime behavior from graph data
Downgrades the risk without new evidence
gold_notes: Risk table: low/medium/high/critical map to explicit review actions.

prompt: Set up an automatic PR review gate in GitHub Actions.
context: Public repository that receives pull requests from forks.
rubric: Uses the composite action `magic5644/Graph-It-Live/.github/actions/graph-it-review-gate` pinned to a version
Checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` so the base ref is available
Disables commenting for fork pull requests instead of exposing a write token to fork code
Sets `fail-on-risk` (high or critical) and bounded `max-depth` / `max-files`
Applies least privilege on `permissions`, dropping `pull-requests: write` when comments are off
anti_patterns: Grants `pull-requests: write` unconditionally on a fork-facing workflow
gold_notes: Action inputs: token, base-ref, comment, fail-on-risk, cli-version, max-depth, max-files. Outputs: risk, score, cli-version.

prompt: review-pr found no test candidates for the changed files. Does that mean tests aren't needed?
context: Repo root: /work/shop, 6 changed files in src/services/.
rubric: States that missing test candidates means manual test selection is required, not that testing is unnecessary
Inspects the actual tests rather than trusting the candidate list
Names concrete verification for the changed behaviour
Includes the gap in the test-assessment section of the review output
anti_patterns: Concludes that no tests are needed
Treats the reported candidate list as complete coverage
gold_notes: Static evidence supplements tests, security review and domain review; it never replaces them.

prompt: The review is timing out — the branch touches almost 500 files.
context: Repo root: /work/platform, branch refactor/di-container, base origin/main.
rubric: Bounds the run with `--max-files` (1-1000) and `--depth` (1-10)
Uses `--format toon` for structured agent analysis of a large report
Warns that bounding raises isPartial and adds limitations that must be reported
Suggests reviewing in slices (per package or per subsystem) rather than dropping analysis
anti_patterns: Bounds the run and then reports the result as complete
gold_notes: --depth 1..10, --max-files 1..1000; bounding is honest only if the limitation is reported.
